title: The Felt and the Sky
working_title: The Unheard: Mongolia / the steppe herders
protagonist: Tuyaa (provisional) — the herder's daughter who left for Ulaanbaatar and is sent back as the survey's face; the crew is secondary POV
unheard_people: the nomadic ger (yurt) herders of the Mongolian steppe (Khalkha — NOT the Kazakh eagle-hunters)
painted_over_word: empty steppe / Genghis cliche / backward herders / underused frontier
fear_of_loss: the herd, the migration, the ger life (mining + dzud + urban drift); the daughter who already lost it once by leaving
antagonist: a composited Gobi copper-and-water mine + its 'empty frontier' fixer; the real weapon is the LAW (herders hold use-right, not title)
jakobus_fire: the long-song (urtiin duu); ALSO the yak/mare-butter-tea + the WRESTLING-HUMBLING + the horse-he-won't-trust beats land here (the humility-engine showcase book)
logline: A herder's daughter who fled a killing winter is sent back as the friendly face of the survey that will fence her father's pasture — and the travelling crew who came for 'the empty land of Genghis' learns the emptiest-looking country on earth is the most precisely known and the most quietly owned.
blueprint: travel-thriller / the unheard place (the relay of attention); single present-day thread, no fantastical layer
market: dignity-first travel-thriller — the unheard, not the cliche
